record.body:
## Description

Teach `discuss` to record what must be true and how it should work before any decision or plan.

## Approach

Decision two-modes. Structured work is a phase that will have a specification. Simple work is incidental, or a phase the user is leaving on pass/fail. `discuss` writes specification and design only for structured work.

In `skills/discuss/SKILL.md`, before the decision step, create one `project:specification` whose subject is the phase slug. Payload `weight`, `phase`, `effort`, `requirements`. `requirements` is the stable ids comma-separated (`R1,R2`). The Requirements section uses those ids (`R1: …`). Use `weight` `light` when the user already fixed the behavior and there is no architectural choice; `full` otherwise. Every required section is present; a section with nothing to say says `none`.

Then create one `project:design` with the same subject. Payload `phase`, `effort`, `decisions` (decision subjects comma-separated). Write the design after the decisions so `decisions` names them. Required sections hold the architecture, interfaces, invariants, assumptions, tradeoffs, and risks. Decisions remain the choices a later reader would re-open.

When an assessment for this phase has `next` `specify`, supersede the specification. When `next` is `design`, supersede the design and any overturned decision, then return to `plan-phase`. Simple work skips both records. Say that in the skill as the two-modes rule.

In `skills/init/SKILL.md`, state that specification and design are written by `discuss`, not `init`.

Update `tests/test_discuss_skill.py` so the write set is `project:specification`, `project:design`, `project:decision`, `project:phase`, and `project:continuity-question`.

The documented `create` and `supersede` payloads must include every required field. Do not edit `plan-phase`, `execute-phase`, or `verify-work`.
